**Best pick: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its 2,073.6 Wh battery and 2,600 W output give you more breathing room than a small backup: the cited estimate is about a day for a 100 W ceramic heat emitter controlled by a thermostat. Actual runtime depends on how often the heater switches on and power-conversion losses. ([specs and runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

For a smaller setup, the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** is listed at 288 Wh; the same source estimates roughly 6–8 hours with a 24 W heat mat. For longer outages—or a higher-wattage heater—the larger station is the safer bet.

Check your heater’s wattage and the station’s AC output before buying. Use the heater with a **reptile thermostat**, and insulate the enclosure to help conserve heat; Petco also recommends insulation as an outage measure. ([Petco outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
